result.note: Cabinet-approved scheme with clear outlay, parks, funding terms and land rules. Tested the scheme's scope, its per-park terms and its outlay split and duration.

questions.prompt: In July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved funding under Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA Rasayan). How many chemical parks does the approval cover?
questions.explain: The Cabinet cleared INR 30.3 billion on 24 July 2026 for three chemical parks. States compete for the three slots through a Challenge Route.
questions.source: The Union Cabinet cleared INR 30.3 billion (USD 314 million) on July 24 for three chemical parks under Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA Rasayan).

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the terms of the BHAVYA Rasayan chemical parks scheme approved in July 2026:
items: The Centre grants up to INR 10 billion per park.
The Central grant is conditional on the host state contributing at least INR 5 billion.
Each site needs a minimum of 8 sq km of contiguous, encumbrance-free land.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three conditions are set out in the scheme's terms, and 8 sq km equals about 2,000 acres. TBB notes that the land and funding gates together favour states that already host chemical capacity.
questions.source: The Centre grants up to INR 10 billion (USD 104 million) per park, conditional on the host state contributing at least INR 5 billion (USD 52 million).

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the BHAVYA Rasayan scheme cleared by the Union Cabinet in July 2026:
items: Of the approved outlay, INR 30 billion is allocated for common infrastructure and utilities inside the parks.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: The scheme runs until 2031, not 2035. Besides the INR 30 billion for shared infrastructure, INR 300 million is earmarked for administration, and the scheme was announced in the 2026 Union Budget.
questions.source: The scheme runs until 2031, and was announced in the 2026 Union Budget.
